Raj — thanks for the clear note and forecast. Short answer: we recommend a mixed-tranche approach that balances lead-time risk against unit-cost. Longer answer below and attached a draft mutual action plan (MAP) for your procurement review.

High-level recommendation (summary):
- Tranche 1 (Oct start): Reserve a small canary of H100-equivalent capacity (10–20% of steady-state peak) to validate network/config and early traffic shaping. Use Redwood Hosted reserved pool or cloud marketplace as immediate backstop.
- Tranche 2 (Nov): Commit the bulk of A100-class reserved capacity (50–60%) to hit predictable unit economics for chat/embedding-heavy workloads.
- Tranche 3 (Dec): Top-up remaining capacity (10–30%) once OEM confirmation on shipment dates is in place, or keep as cloud-burst capacity if OEM slips.

SKU rationale:
- H100 lanes for low-latency, high-throughput model variants (LLM-70B+). Higher per-unit perf but longer OEM lead-time and higher price.
- A100 (or equivalent) lanes for lower-cost embedding/embedding-batch workloads where latency SLO is looser. Faster OEM availability in many cases.

Lead-time expectations (ballpark):
- OEM direct fulfillment: 10–16 weeks from PO (varies by SKU and global queue).
- Cloud reserved marketplace/backstop: 1–3 weeks provisioning but subject to regional capacity and higher unit costs.

Recommended actions for NovusAI procurement:
1) Confirm priority SKU per workload slice by Aug 2 (so we can lock OEM quoting lanes).
2) Sign the attached MAP to tier commitments and milestone POs (link included in MAP).
3) Provide a firm expected steady-state peak and acceptable cost delta for cloud fallback.

Attachments: NovusAI_MutualActionPlan_draft.pdf, sku-tranche-matrix.xlsx (worksheet with suggested splits).

I'll loop Marissa and Ben to coordinate vendor negotiation and OEM quote capture. Happy to jump on a 30-min call this week.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
